name: Bianco Capena

climate: Seasons this warm ripen Carignan, Zinfandel and Nebbiolo fully without cooking off their freshness.
Merlot is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Sangiovese is at its warm limit. It can ripen too fast, giving heavy, soft wine that has lost its freshness.
Rain picks up at harvest. Growers race to pick before rot sets in, and vintages vary more.

soil.rock: Volcanic rock is porous, so it drains well and sends roots deep. Lava soils are mostly basalt, rich in iron, calcium and magnesium. Limestone makes alkaline soil that drains well yet can hold water for the vines. It is usually planted to grapes valued for their acidity.
soil.top: The topsoil holds water well and drains at a steady pace, so vines rarely go thirsty or sit in wet ground. Its high pH can starve vines of iron and yellow the leaves, so growers plant lime-tolerant rootstocks.

land: The high ground runs about 3°F cooler than the low ground. Higher vineyards ripen later and keep more acidity, so one grape can make lighter or richer wine here depending on height.
Gentle slopes. Enough tilt to drain cold air and rain away, which lowers frost risk, yet still easy to farm by machine.

winkler: Big crops are possible, but quality tops out at acceptable.
